title: The four directions' wind-ups and ready poses: how a held blow is cocked, and how long the wind-up and the strike take
note: Ours, not the rules package's: every number here is ENGINE_SANDBOX. The wind-ups for all four directions, with Mount & Blade's 'hold attack, and then switch movements to change the attack direction'. Each blow plays: press -> its wind-up into its ready pose (held there while attack is held: the ready point is the wind-up's end) -> the strike from that pose (the blow's own clip from strike_from_frame; the blade its own again by join_at_frame, so its path through the active window is the earlier builds') -> the recovery. Times are 1.1's frames (30 a second) of the blow, played at the blow's own rate (the weapon's: 1.1 stretches an attack so the whole clip takes its STRIKETIME; the broadsword plays 0.88 frames a frame, so 9 frames are 0.34 s): wind_up_frames from the press to the ready pose; strike_frames from the ready pose to the clip's end (-1: as the blow plays them, its frames strike_from_frame to its end). The wind-ups take as long as each blow took to its ready point before (7, 9, 11 and 13 frames), so the pace is unchanged until the pace survey: combat was far too fast. Places are in the kind's model space before the aim offset bends the upper body (metres; +X its right, +Y its front, +Z up, the feet at 0), for 1.1's skeleton 0 (Christof, the guards, the watchmen: the same bones): guard is where the ready pose holds the blade's guard, blade the way the blade points from it, via the control point of the guard's curve from the stance, turn_degrees the upper body turned to its left (negative: its right) at the ready pose. Read by the session (OneOneWindUps); the platform's own numbers (OneOneWindUps.Defaults) are these.
